# LOADING PACKAGES.
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
library(tidyverse)

theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(text = element_text(size = 15)))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# LOAD IN DATA.
```{r LOAD IN DATA}
# Create dataframe "data" which contains cleaned participant data without pure controls.
data <- read_csv('../Data/data_cleaned.csv') # Read csv data file.
```

# CALCULATE PROPORTIONS.
```{r CALCULATE PROPORTIONS}
# Create dataframe "future_use_control" which calculates the proportion of future platform use responses in the control condition.
future_use_control <- data %>% 
  filter(condition == "control") %>% # Filter for participants in the control condition.
  count(future_use) %>% # Count the number of participants who selected each future use response.
  mutate(proportion = prop.table(n)*100) # Calculate the proportion of future use responses.

# Create column "Experimental Condition" which indicates the experimental condition.
future_use_control <- future_use_control %>% 
  mutate(`Experimental Condition` = "Control") # Experimental condition was control.

# Create dataframe "future_use_treatment" which calculates the proportion of future platform use responses in the treatment condition.
future_use_treatment <- data %>% 
  filter(condition == "treat") %>% # Filter for participants in the treatment condition.
  count(future_use) %>% # Count the number of participants who selected each future use response.
  mutate(proportion = prop.table(n)*100) # Calculate the proportion of future use responses.

# Create column "Experimental Condition" which indicates the experimental condition.
future_use_treatment <- future_use_treatment %>% 
  mutate(`Experimental Condition` = "Treat") # Experimental condition was treatment.
```

# FORMAT TABLE.
```{r FORMAT TABLE}
# Combine future_use_control and future_use_treatment into a new dataframe "table7".
table7 <- rbind(future_use_control, future_use_treatment)

# Delete the column "n" which contains the count information for participants within each category.
table7["n"] <- NULL

# Round the proportions to two decimal places.
table7 <- table7 %>% 
  mutate(proportion = round(proportion, 2))

# Reorganize the table.
table7 <- table7 %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = future_use, values_from = proportion) # The future use response categories are the new columns, and contain the proportions. The rows are the experimental conditions.

# Rename the first column.
colnames(table7)[1] <- c(" ") # Rename the first column with a blank space " ".

# Reorder the columns.
table7 <- table7[c(" ", "Very unlikely", "Somewhat unlikely", "Neither unlikely nor likely", "Somewhat likely", "Very likely")] # Define the order of the columns, listing column names in order of preferred appearance.
```

# FINAL TABLE.
```{r FINAL TABLE}
print(table7)
stargazer::stargazer(table7, rownames = FALSE, summary = FALSE)
```


# FINAL TEST STATISTIC
```{r FINAL TEST STATISTIC}
# Cohen's d with pooled SD (classic, equal-variance pooling)
cohen_d <- function(x, y) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]; y <- y[!is.na(y)]
  nx <- length(x); ny <- length(y)
  sp <- sqrt(((nx - 1) * var(x) + (ny - 1) * var(y)) / (nx + ny - 2))
  (mean(x) - mean(y)) / sp
}
 

y_tx <- data[data$condition == 'treat', ]$future_use_numeric >= 3
y_ct <- data[data$condition == 'control', ]$future_use_numeric >= 3
tt <- t.test(y_tx, y_ct)               # Welch's t-test (unequal variances)

outcome <- 'future_use'
n_yes <- sum(!is.na(y_tx))
n_no <- sum(!is.na(y_ct))
mean_yes <- mean(y_tx, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_no <- mean(y_ct, na.rm = TRUE)
d <- cohen_d(y_tx, y_ct)
t <- unname(tt$statistic)
df <- unname(tt$parameter)
p <- tt$p.value

cat('We tested whether participants in the treated condition were more likely than those in the control condition to report being "somewhat likely" or "very likely" to use the platform again. Using a two-sided Welch\'s t-test,  we found that $',round(mean_yes*100, 0),'\\%$ of participants in the treated group were likely to use the platform again compared to only $', round(mean_no*100, 0), '\\% $ of subjects in the control group $(d=', round(d, 3), 
', t = ', round(t, 3),
',df = ', round(df, 3), 
',P = ', round(p, 3), ')$')



```
